  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The regression test embeds comment JSON containing backticks in a Bash double-quoted assignment, so Bash executes the marker text as command substitution and corrupts the test input.
  WHY: The test fails in CI; reviewers disagreed on severity between BLOCKER and MAJOR, so the highest severity is used.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2259-2261 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `count_identical_failures` recognizes cap markers anywhere in a comment body, including inside “First error” text, unlike the line-anchored checks.
  WHY: An inline current-head, current-support marker can make the gate skip posting a real cap marker, while the poller does not recognize it and re-dispatches the review.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2209-2230 | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `parse_failure_markers` and `count_identical_failures` scan the entire comment body, including text within `First error:` quotes.
  WHY: Markers embedded in error messages can be misidentified as primary failures, causing incorrect cap states or failure counts and potentially blocking needed PR re-dispatches.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:2529; scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26142 | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The workflow and poller cap-marker regexes interpret the trailing anchor differently.
  WHY: The poller's regex can match a literal `$` rather than end-of-string, making cap detection differ depending on whether the marker ends with a newline.

  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_noop_suspicious_recovery.py:641-649

- requirement: "Update the poller's cap-marker check to use the same rule. This lets the scheduled sweep retry previously capped PRs without disabling the cap for new failures."
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26142 regex consistency
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]

- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2259-2260 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  File: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py
  Line or code reference: 2259-2260
  PROBLEM: `count_identical_failures` finds cap markers anywhere in a comment body, unlike the line-anchored workflow and poller jq checks.
  WHY: An inline marker with the current head and support SHA can set `cap_applied=true` in the Python parser while remaining invisible to the jq checks, causing the gate and poller to diverge.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Make the failure streak and cap markers version-aware using the verified review-support SHA. Ignore markers from older support versions when evaluating a review with updated support, and update the poller's cap-marker check to use the same rule."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2259 (count_identical_failures cap-marker detection)
  Evidence of absence: The gate's Python path (`count_identical_failures`, line 2259) uses `re.search()` which matches cap markers anywhere in the comment body, while the workflow's jq (`review_autofix.yml:2529`) and poller's jq (`orchestrate_poll_process.sh:26142`) both use `(^|\n)` line anchoring. The agents.md paragraph added by this PR says "the gate, the cap job and the sweep ignore markers of another or no support version" — implying all three use one rule. But `count_identical_failures` has no line-anchoring guard, so an inline cap marker in a pipeline-authored failure comment can set `cap_applied=true` in the gate's Python path while remaining invisible to the poller and cap-job jq paths. The three paths are not using the same rule.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

The other six new cap-skip tests all pass. The backtick command-substitution issue described under CORRECTNESS & LOGIC causes the failure.
